openThreads: VOCABULARY GAP (the instruction is wrong here, or at least underspecified): the fixed state set has no value for 'instrument located and its dimensional table confirmed to exist, extraction not completed'. Roughly a third of this lane's cities are in exactly that condition. I used `blocked` for them and named the wall in each note, but `blocked` as the brief defines it means 'a real instrument appears to exist but you were prevented from reaching it', and in several of those cases I was not prevented by the source -- I was prevented by this lane's own remaining capacity, with the text one rendering step away. Either add an 'identified-not-extracted'/'handoff' state, or read this lane's `blocked` entries as a queue rather than as walls. The cities that are true, source-level walls are Wimberley (client-rendered current text vs a stale 2022 print), Florence (unexecuted exhibit -- blank ordinance number and date), Coupland (registered host resolves to Cedar Park), Niederwald/Weir/Hays/Staples (hosts did not answer), and Mountain City/Bartlett/Woodcreek (client-rendered code bodies).

Wimberley is the biggest open acquisition in the lane after Jarrell: 2,273 parcels, a ~30-district table in Sec. 9.03.071 - Sec. 9.03.101 that must be read from a rendered page, with two wrinkles (height stated as two values by roof type; standards subordinate to Sec. 9.03.184(a) Table A where the larger governs). Do not code it off the 2022-05-13 city print without a currency check against the code that is current through Ord. 2025-21 (adopted 2025-11-06).

Woodcreek is a category-1 city (a staged layer we already hold, 1,026 parcels with no setback row) whose table is confirmed -- the largest false-absence block in this lane's scope. Its district vocabulary (Table 1 of the census) mixes Single Family 1-6, Recreational, Fourplex, TH/C, Natural Preserve, Government, Neighborhood Commercial and a Planned Development class that must route to the PUD refusal. Highest priority for the next acquisition pass.

Jarrell's table leaves two questions deliberately open: (a) the impervious-cover/lot-coverage standards live in Chapter 6.00 'Site Development and Design Standards', which this lane did not extract -- the fields are not_specified, not absent; (b) the city's own development document page exposes no downloadable exhibit for Ordinance 2024-0206-01, so a reconciling read of the executed Chapter 4 against the mirror used here is still owed.

Martindale's currency is unverified: the authoritative host (codelibrary.amlegal.com) returns 403 to this lane, so the code's 'current through' date could not be read and a post-2013 amendment to Sec. 155.076 - Sec. 155.084 cannot be ruled out. Values are coded at 0.85 for that reason. A rendering-capable read should close it.

Registry defect to fix: tx-coupland's source pointer (ecode360.com/CE6271) resolves to the City of Cedar Park's code. Anything that trusted that pointer for Coupland is wrong. Also worth correcting: tx-weir's own note says its source URL is unconfirmed, and tx-uhland's Municode listing is a stub -- both need a resolution pass before the next lane can classify them.

Florence's published exhibit is unexecuted (blank ordinance number and adoption date in the enacting clause).
